angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 81,396,900 km at 4139.40 pc = 0.26 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, VX Per: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 4139.4 +/- 483.6 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 4139.4 +/- 483.6 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 0.3636 +/- 0.0168 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12), 21.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 117 +/- 13.8 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, VX Per: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 117 +/- 13.8 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 81,396,900 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5375 +/- 208 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 251, Name='VX Per', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5375 +/- 208 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 251, Name='VX Per', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5375 +/- 208 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186)
surfaceGravitySource: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, VizieR J/AJ/156/171/table11, recno 39, Name='VX Per', column Gavg ('Average gravity over cycle'; log g in dex, ReadMe unit label cm/s2): log g 1.64 averaged over the pulsation cycle (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..171L)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* VX Per: spectral type G2IV (1978A&AS...32...25R)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* VX Per: main object type cC*, Classical Cepheid Variable

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
